grade.primary_choice: Don't rewrite now; measure, tune and scale Reverb horizontally with a week-3 decision gate
ruled_out_recommended: Switching to a non-Pusher protocol (Centrifugo) inside the 3-month window, offered as the conditional 'best fallback' at the week-3 gate
red_flags_hit: Recommends a protocol change (Centrifugo, which needs new client libraries and a new auth flow) as the main fallback inside the 3-month window, though only if a measured test fails
Leaves out load-balancer WebSocket limits and timeouts, and Redis as a single point of failure for availability (it mentions only Redis throughput limits)
unsupported_claims: 'Many teams run well past that on PHP-based WebSocket servers' is a vague claim with nothing to back it
grade.notes: The answer is strong and well grounded: no rewrite before the deadline, measure first, ext-uv instead of stream_select with its ~1,024 limit, Redis scaling, a 100k+ load test with reconnect storms, cost compared with managed services, and the bus-factor risk. It falls short by naming Centrifugo, a protocol change, as the main fallback inside the deadline instead of Soketi or a managed Pusher-compatible service. It also never says Reverb is single-threaded, so it misses running several processes per VM, and it skips load-balancer timeouts and N+1 capacity planning.
